BLASTr searches many sequences with BLAST+ from R and returns the hits ranked, a summary per sequence and the consensus lowest common ancestor of the best hits, with the NCBI taxonomy.
This vignette goes from a FASTA file to a summary per sequence, with the small database that comes with the package.
It runs in a few seconds and needs no internet.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(BLASTr)
```

## Install

BLASTr is installed from GitHub; BLAST+ is installed by `install_dependencies()` in a conda environment of its own (`blastr-blast-env`), through the condathis package, so it does not depend on what is installed on the system.

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("heronoh/BLASTr")
BLASTr::install_dependencies()
```

The code below runs only where BLAST+ is available.

```{r}
#| label: has-blast
has_blast <- nzchar(Sys.which("blastn"))
has_blast
```

## A BLAST database from a FASTA file

`make_blast_db()` formats a FASTA file as a BLAST database.
The package has a small one, `minimal_db_blast.fasta`, with 47 GenBank sequences.
For real analyses, `download_blast_db()` downloads any database of the NCBI (such as `core_nt`) with the taxonomy of the same date, and `make_unite_db()` and `make_silva_db()` build UNITE and SILVA as BLAST databases (see their help pages).

```{r}
#| label: make-db
#| eval: !expr has_blast
fasta <- system.file("extdata", "minimal_db_blast.fasta", package = "BLASTr")
db <- file.path(tempdir(), "minimal_db_blast")
make_blast_db(fasta, db_path = db)
```

## Searching

`parallel_blast()` takes a character vector of sequences and the path of the database.
It chooses how to split the search (how many `blastn` processes, threads per process and sequences per batch) from the size of the database and the cores (`total_cores`) and RAM available; `blast_strategy()` shows the choice before the search.

```{r}
#| label: search
#| eval: !expr has_blast
seqs <- readLines(system.file("extdata", "seqs_test.txt", package = "BLASTr"))
length(seqs)
blast_strategy(n_seqs = length(seqs), db_path = db, total_cores = 2)
res <- parallel_blast(seqs, db, total_cores = 2)
```

By default, BLAST keeps up to 50 subjects per sequence (`search_alignments`) with at least 80% identity (`perc_id`) and 50% query coverage (`search_qcov_hsp`).

## Reading the results

The result has one row per hit, best first, and one row with empty hit fields for each sequence without hits:

```{r}
#| label: columns
#| eval: !expr has_blast
res[, c("Sequence", "rank", "tie", "at_best", "subject", "identity", "qcovhsp", "Similarity score", "low_qcov")]
```

- `Similarity score` is `(10 * identity + qcovhsp) / 11` (see `similarity_score()`). The hits are ranked by it (`rank_by = "similarity"`), then by identity, coverage, bitscore and BLAST order. `blast_rank` keeps the order of BLAST, which favours longer alignments.
- `at_best` marks the hits within `check_tolerance` (0.5 points) of the best one: the tied candidates for the identification. `tie` marks hits with the same value as another one.
- `low_qcov` marks hits that cover less than `perc_qcov_hsp` (80%) of the sequence; they are kept and ranked, but the identification of a sequence whose best hit has `low_qcov` rests on a partial alignment.
- `informative` is `FALSE` for references that do not inform the identification (uncultured, environmental, metagenomes, vectors...; see `uninformative_references()`); they get no `rank` and come after the informative hits.
- The first 10 ranked hits (`num_alignments`) are kept, plus all the hits at best.

## One row per sequence

`blast_summary()` summarises the hits of each sequence:

```{r}
#| label: summary
#| eval: !expr has_blast
blast_summary(res)
```

`Check ID` is `"best ID"` when all the hits at best among the first 10 have the taxid of the first hit, and `"check ID"` otherwise (another taxid, or an unknown one, as here: the example database has no taxids).
`At best truncated` is `TRUE` when the last subject BLAST returned is tied with the best one, so more tied subjects may exist beyond `search_alignments`.

## Taxonomy and the lowest common ancestor

With a database that has taxids (`download_blast_db()`, `make_unite_db()`, `make_silva_db()`, or `make_blast_db(taxid_map = )`), `get_tax()` adds the NCBI taxonomy of each taxid from a local SQLite database, built once from the NCBI taxdump of the date of the BLAST database, and `blast_lca()` gives the deepest taxon that contains at least 90% of the hits tied with the best one:

```{r}
#| label: taxonomy
#| eval: false
tax <- get_tax(res)
dplyr::left_join(res, tax, by = c(staxid = "taxid"))
lca <- blast_lca(res)
```

The help pages of `get_tax()` and `blast_lca()` have examples that run with a small taxonomy written on the spot.
